title: Ukraine launches a counteroffensive in Kharkiv Oblast
body:
Ukraine launched a counteroffensive in Kharkiv Oblast on 6 September 2022, shortly after announcing a separate offensive in the south near Kherson. Ukrainian forces broke through thinly held Russian lines in the east. Fighting in Balakliia ended on 8 September, though Ukraine did not establish full control there until 10 September, and Shevchenkove was retaken on 8 September.

On 10 September Ukrainian troops retook Izium and Kupiansk, securing access to the Oskil River. On 11 September the Russian Ministry of Defence announced a withdrawal from nearly all of Kharkiv Oblast, and by 13 September Ukraine had retaken the oblast west of the Oskil. Ukrainian forces crossed the river around 13 September and held bridgeheads on the east bank. They retook Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi on 26 September.

The advance continued into Donetsk Oblast, where Lyman was encircled in late September and captured on 1 October. Early in the offensive the Institute for the Study of War estimated that about 2,500 square kilometres had been retaken. Later accounts put the total at more than 500 settlements and about 12,000 square kilometres in the Kharkiv region. The article records the outcome as a Ukrainian victory.
